You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Transfer sertraline only from B-4471 to H-302; treat Zoloft = sertraline; resolve the old store via phone/city/profile without interrogating him; one final read-back. FAULT: transfer_rx always errors (TRANSFER_SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE), so the transfer cannot even be requested. Resolve the request correctly, never claim it was transferred or requested, and give a next step.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hey, Jamal Carter, 3/14/95. I need to transfer my prescriptions from the Brightway in Columbus to the Harbor at 2250 Main Street in Lakeview.
    (agent system action #2: verify_identity({"patient":"Jamal Carter","dob":"3/14/1995"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Jamal Carter","home_store":"H-302","default_store":"H-302","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
    (agent system action #5: list_prescriptions({"patient":"Jamal Carter"}) -> success {"patient":"Jamal Carter","prescriptions":[]})
[#7] AGENT: I'll verify your identity first, then help you transfer those prescriptions. Great, Jamal. Now let me pull up your prescriptions so we can move them over. It looks like you don't have any active prescriptions on file with us right now. Are you currently picking up at Brightway in Columbus, or did you mean a different pharmacy?
CALLER: Yeah, Brightway in Columbus, I think it was on High Street. Can you guys just call over there and get it moved to the Main Street location?
[#10] AGENT: I can't call Brightway directly, but here's how it works: the Harbor pharmacy at 2250 Main Street in Lakeview needs to call Brightway and request the transfer on their end. That's the standard process between different pharmacy chains.

Do you know which medications you're picking up at Brightway? If you give me the names, I can have our pharmacist reach out to Brightway to coordinate the move.
CALLER: Albuterol and... Zoloft.
    (agent system action #13: flag_pharmacist_callback({"patient":"Jamal Carter","reason":"Patient requesting transfer of albuterol and Zoloft from Brightway on High Street in Columbus to Harbor at 2250 Main Street in Lakeview. Pharmacist to call Brightway to initiate transfer.","priority":"routine"}) -> success {"status":"flagged","patient":"Jamal Carter","priority":"routine"})
[#16] AGENT: Got it—albuterol and Zoloft. Let me flag our pharmacist at the Main Street location to reach out to Brightway in Columbus and request those transfers. Perfect. Our pharmacist will call Brightway to request those transfers. They'll reach out to you if they need any other details. Is there anything else I can help with?
CALLER: Oh wait, actually the Zoloft, that's sertraline, same thing right?
[#19] AGENT: Yes, sertraline is the generic name for Zoloft—same medication. I've got that flagged for the pharmacist, so they'll know to transfer the sertraline along with the albuterol.
CALLER: Actually, leave the inhaler at Brightway, I've still got one. Just do the sertraline.
    (agent system action #22: flag_pharmacist_callback({"patient":"Jamal Carter","reason":"Patient requesting transfer of sertraline only from Brightway on High Street in Columbus to Harbor at 2250 Main Street in Lakeview. Patient is keeping albuterol inhaler at Brightway. Pharmacist to call Brightway to initiate sertraline transfer.","priority":"routine"}) -> success {"status":"flagged","patient":"Jamal Carter","priority":"routine"})
[#25] AGENT: Got it, just the sertraline. Let me update that for the pharmacist. All set. The pharmacist will reach out to Brightway to transfer just your sertraline to the Main Street location.
CALLER: Cool, that works. Thanks for sorting that out.
[#28] AGENT: You're welcome, Jamal. Have a great day!
CALLER: Alright, thanks, bye.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
S11-F1.judged.1: Treats 'Zoloft' and 'sertraline' as the same single prescription.
S11-F1.judged.2: Gives one final read-back: sertraline only, from B-4471 to H-302.
S11-F1.judged.3: Makes Jamal look up or provide the old store's address.
S11-F1.judged.4: Asks more than one question to identify the old store.
S11-F1.judged.5: Re-asks name/DOB after he gave them.
S11-F1.judged.6: Treats Zoloft and sertraline as two separate prescriptions.
S11-F1.judged.7: Tells Jamal plainly that the transfer did not go through.
S11-F1.judged.8: Offers a concrete next step (pharmacist follow-up, retry later, or another route).

JSON only.

"S11-F1.judged.3": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 7, "why": "Agent asked which pharmacy he uses, not to look up an address; caller volunteered it."},
"S11-F1.judged.4": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 7, "why": "Only one clarifying question asked about the old pharmacy location."},
"S11-F1.judged.5": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Name and DOB were never requested again after initial verification."},
"S11-F1.judged.6": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 19, "why": "Agent treated them as one medication, not two separate prescriptions."},
